_notes: Poly Haven publishes NO .glb files for these assets. Its 'gltf' category is an uncompressed multi-file bundle: <id>_1k.gltf + <id>.bin + textures/*.jpg. Each downloaded asset is therefore a directory bundle, loadable directly by the vendored three.js GLTFLoader via 'assets/models/<id>/<id>_1k.gltf'.
No Draco or KTX2 extensions are used, so nothing is required beyond vendor/GLTFLoader.js to load them.
All four downloaded assets use the 1k LOD (the lowest offered) and every file was MD5-verified against the Poly Haven API.

The three tree assets were skipped because even their smallest download is 96-914 MB. They are photogrammetry scans with extremely dense meshes; fixing them requires mesh decimation (gltfpack/meshoptimizer or a Blender decimate pass), not a smaller download.

fir_tree_01.reason: No .glb exists for this asset, and the glTF export is an uncompressed multi-file bundle (.gltf + .bin + 11 textures). The geometry alone (fir_tree_01.bin) is 456 MB, making the smallest possible download ~465 MB at the 1k LOD - far above the 6 MB cap.

pine_tree_01.reason: No .glb exists for this asset, and the glTF export is an uncompressed multi-file bundle (.gltf + .bin + 11 textures). The geometry alone (pine_tree_01.bin) is 905 MB, making the smallest possible download ~914 MB at the 1k LOD - far above the 6 MB cap.

tree_small_02.reason: No .glb exists for this asset, and the glTF export is an uncompressed multi-file bundle (.gltf + .bin + 9 textures). The geometry alone (tree_small_02.bin) is 91 MB, making the smallest possible download ~96 MB at the 1k LOD - far above the 6 MB cap.
